title: Deterministic work queue simulator
prompt: Build a CLI reading a JSON array of jobs from stdin and simulating one worker in logical time, starting at t=0, without real sleeping. A job is {id,priority,available_at,duration,fail_attempts,max_attempts}: id unique nonempty string; priority integer (higher runs first); available_at integer >= 0; duration integer >= 1; fail_attempts integer >= 0, the number of initial attempts that fail; max_attempts integer >= 1. Any other shape, duplicate ids or invalid JSON: exit nonzero, leave stdout empty and write a diagnostic to stderr. Simulation: at time t the ready jobs are unfinished, not permanently failed jobs whose available_at is at most t. If none are ready, jump t to the smallest available_at among the remaining jobs; when no job remains the simulation ends. Run the ready job with the highest priority, ties broken by id in plain code-unit string order. Its attempt number n (1-based) occupies [t,t+duration); the attempt fails when n <= fail_attempts, otherwise it succeeds. After the attempt t becomes t+duration. A failed job with n >= max_attempts is permanently failed; any other failed job becomes ready again at available_at = t + 10*n (t after the attempt). Print exactly one JSON object and a newline: {events,final,end_time}: events lists every attempt in order as {job,attempt,start,end,outcome} with outcome "success" or "fail"; final maps each job id to "finished" or "failed"; end_time is t when the simulation ends (0 for no jobs). Exit 0 on success. No external services are needed.
